recentItems.title: Behind The Scenes At The Arqana Yearling Sale | The Bloodstock Files
recentItems.description:
The Bloodstock Files goes to Deauville for the Arqana August Yearling Sale, the first of the European season — and hands the episode to Emma Berry and Bernard Condren in their day jobs as journalist and auctioneer.

Bernard walks his lots in the morning, explaining what he looks for in a yearling, why the walk matters, and how twenty-six years of auctioneering started with bit-spotting at Goffs while he should have been at school. Then, wearing camera glasses on the rostrum, he sells a Justify colt for €1.25 million with Godolphin and Coolmore going toe to toe, and follows it with a Wootton Bassett colt at €800,000.

Emma is out with the TDN team, and talks to Henri Bozo, director at Ecurie des Monceaux. Plus Pierre Boulard, Willie Mullins's man in France, on why they're now buying flat yearlings with enough stamina and scope to jump if the flat doesn't work out.

#TheBloodstockFiles #Bloodstock #horseracing

recentItems.title: The Verdict: Sprint Cup Analysis | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Angus McNae and Josh Kerr go through the week's action with the RaceIQ sectional data, headed by Almeraq's win in the Betfair Sprint Cup.

Almeraq is the World Pool Race of the Week, beating Paborus with last year's winner Big Mojo third — though the clock has a view on how the race was run, with a time index of 3.1 against a meeting average of 4.9 and a winning time nearly two seconds above par.

Also from Haydock on Saturday, First Law broke fastest of all and quickened through three very fast furlongs to win the Ascendant Stakes from Rocket Boy, and Aegean Prince was cruising three out before landing the Old Borough Cup.

Plus the fastest performances of the week away from the Group 1 — Pride Of Arras posting the best time index of the lot at Kempton on Saturday, Fortitudine going quicker than par over a mile and three at Kempton on Wednesday, and Sharaad at Haydock on Thursday, who switched leads inside the final furlong and took some pulling up.

recentItems.title: Bryan Cooper On Don Cossack, Gigginstown & Life After Riding | On The Wire On The Road
recentItems.description:
On The Wire On The Road continues its three-part series around Irish racing, as Andrew Blair White sits down with a Gold Cup-winning jockey who has swapped the weighing room for the sales ring. 

Bryan Cooper walked into Dessie Hughes's yard at fourteen and spent the first evening picking stones. He was a stable jockey at eighteen and riding for Gigginstown at twenty-one, sitting across a table from Michael O'Leary asking for terms. 

He talks about the 2013 Cheltenham Festival treble, walking the track with Gordon Elliott on Gold Cup morning in 2016, and why he chose Don Cossack over Don Poli. 

Bryan shares about losing the Gigginstown job, retiring at Cheltenham after a fall when he'd planned to finish at Punchestown, and what nobody tells you about life after riding. 

Now he buys horses for a handful of owners and helps his father at home in Kerry.

#BryanCooper #horseracing #goldcup

recentItems.title: Extremely Zain Bounces Back In Style In The Garrowby Stakes | Replay | Racing TV
recentItems.description:
Extremely Zain provided William Haggas with back-to-back wins in the Starman At Tally Ho Stud Garrowby Stake at York. 

Just 24 hours on from Almeraq's scintillating win in the Betfair Sprint Cup, team Haggas were celebrating once again as the Cieren Fallon-ridden colt - who had been doing most of his racing over further - relished the relative test of stamina to land the listed sprint and follow in the footsteps of last year's winning stablemate Elmonjed. 

The Andrew Balding-trained Double Rush was a well-backed favourite and held every chance a furlong from home under Shane Foley, but was unable to peg back the winner, with Kevin 

Ryan's Dickensian staying on well from off the pace to pip the front-running Regional for third. 
Fallon told Racing TV: "He's a very good horse and he's shown a lot of speed. It was a bold decision to come back to six and the right one. 

"He can just be in your hands a little bit and at Ascot you can't get away with it. On his homework as well we decided to come back 

"They go faster so you can settle easier."
